analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Credit in focus & shorts scale; this week's preview; SES to BUY; Nvidia pushing memory names to standardise
key_insights: US equities fell last week on hotter inflation, higher oil prices and AI-trade concerns. Semis fell for an eighth consecutive session, memory weakened sharply and crowded momentum trades kept unwinding.

Global Tech saw its largest percentage net selling on record since 2016, with semis 57% of US technology net selling. Essentially all of the fall in hedge fund net exposure since the end of July came from added shorts, not reduced longs.
Fundamental long/short managers were down 2.7% for the week. Global books had their largest net selling since the end of July, led by record selling in Information Technology.
The debate has broadened to rates, AI capex returns, China competition and whether the market overestimated the durability of AI infrastructure bottlenecks, and is less about Q3 earnings.
Lee Copperfield flagged Friday as the first real sign of panic in index protection. VIX futures traded 3.6x the 20-day average.

The biggest incremental development is the move in credit. AI-related credit spreads, especially for neoclouds and companies exposed to frontier AI labs, widened, and neoclouds fell about 25% on the week. Most see AI demand itself as fine.
Investors question how parts of the AI ecosystem will fund capex if funding costs stay elevated. The Telegraph reported over the weekend that MSFT is backing away from a Neocloud deal.

With AI capex growth potentially past its peak, credit quality, funding needs and ROIC are becoming more important to equity valuations. The coming earnings season is a test of whether fundamentals can stop the sentiment and momentum deterioration.

Nvidia is pushing Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron to use TSMC's 3nm process for NVHBM base dies. Near-term P&L impact on memory names should be limited because they keep turnkey production for standard HBM. Strategically it is positive for TSMC and shifts control of HBM architecture toward Nvidia.

GIR reinstated coverage of SES at Buy (EUR7.0 PT, 79% upside to base case, >180% in blue-sky) on C-band cash and space-defence spending. Eutelsat is Neutral (EUR1.6 PT) on execution risk, capital intensity, LEO competition and limited cash generation until post-2030.

FT reports Accenture is looking to sell its Greater China operations for up to $1.5bn, unconfirmed, possibly keeping a significant minority stake. The company forecasts 3% to 6% revenue growth for FY2027.

Gavin Baker (on X, echoed on the AllIn podcast) argues OpenAI's compute contracts are well below current spot compute prices and hyperscalers will see revenue growth accelerate as contracts reprice. He thinks external financing as a share of the AI buildout may be nearing its peak.

SAP preview: sentiment is now more constructive and closer to a consensus long. Current cloud backlog (CCB) is the swing factor. GIR keeps about 23% organic CCB growth ex-FX for 3Q26, a 22% exit rate in 4Q and about 24% FY26 cloud revenue growth ex-FX, in line with guidance.

META is up 40% from its August lows after the Muse release. GIR forecasts higher 2027 opex and capex than the Street, with revenue in line for Q3/FY26 and 2.4% ahead for 2027. Results come slightly earlier than normal, prompting questions about a possible equity raise.

Analog: TXN reports first. GS expects about 3% revenue upside, a 4Q guide about 2% above Street and CY26 EPS about 2% above Street. The stock is about -6% in CY3Q26 vs about -10% for the peer average. Watch 300mm fab utilization, auto/industrial restocking and the $8/share 2026 FCF target.

BESI sentiment is increasingly negative after two broker downgrades and a SemiAnalysis report arguing hybrid-bonding adoption in HBM is slower than expected and ASML could enter die-to-wafer bonding. Q3 orders may still beat, but BESI is likely to remain a funding short.

US telcos: Verizon is forecast at Q3 revenue $35.0bn and EBITDA $13.8bn, with 2026 FCF up 10.5% to $22.2bn. AT&T is forecast at revenue $31.8bn, EBITDA $12.5bn and 416k postpaid phone adds. The debate is pricing, convergence economics and Starlink's spectrum acquisition.

Nordic telecoms: Tele2 has the most interesting Q3 setup. Telia is on track. Elisa Q3 is in line with Q2 and the shares remain a consensus short. Telenor (reports week after next) looks like a consensus short on weak Norway competition, energy costs and Bangladesh.

Pearson: Q3 organic growth is expected to accelerate to about 5.5%. Cevian's stake raises the question of a Higher Education separation. At about 15x forward earnings the risk/reward is balanced. Short interest is 6.8% of free float, about 19 days to cover.

RELX: 9M26 organic growth expected around 7% (Risk 8%, Legal 10%, STM 6%, Exhibitions 4%). GIR thinks the market is too bearish on AI disruption since Legal is 12% of group EBIT. The stock trades at 17x 2027E EPS.
Spotify Q3 preview: revenue of EUR4.96bn expected, slightly below guidance and consensus of EUR5.0bn, with 305m Premium subscribers and 788m MAUs. Buy retained, PT cut to $645 from $655.

TSMC is accelerating advanced-node expansion (A14 risk production 2027, mass production 2028; Arizona Fab 2 toward 3Q27 mass production). Japan approved the 3nm upgrade at the second Kumamoto fab with up to US$4.1bn in support. The Samsung-TSMC NVHBM collaboration is a media report, not a confirmed award.
GIR raised global server TAM by 31% / 45% in 2027 / 28E. AI server shipments are raised, implying AI chip demand of 18m / 29m / 38m in 2026-28E and about 60% / 50% ASIC penetration in 2028E.
Japan electronics/semis: GIR prefers Murata, Taiyo Yuden, TDK, Renesas, Rohm and Ibiden, and upgrades Nichicon to Buy on AI server capacitor demand.
Americas emerging software: Zeta upgraded to Buy from Neutral (up 65% YTD, 4x risk/reward skew) and Klaviyo downgraded to Neutral from Buy.
Apple's foldable iPhone Duo goes on sale Oct 23 with initial Taiwan shipments of just over 10,000 units, possibly short of preorder demand.

Credit and restructuring items: Virgin Media O2 carries about EUR/GBP 22bn of debt (GBP22bn) and is weighing a low-cost tier, while CityFibre asked banks to write down a significant part of its GBP2bn loan for equity.

market_movers.rationale: Attractive entry after recent weakness, with upside from incoming C-band cash and higher space-defence spending. 79% upside to base case and >180% in blue-sky.
Eutelsat faces execution risk, a capital-intensive model, LEO competition and limited cash generation until post-2030.
Greater visibility into upside to 2027 estimates, enterprise share gains and a 4x risk/reward skew. Shares are up 65% YTD.
Less visibility into the timing and magnitude of newer growth drivers despite a positive long-term view.
Nichicon upgraded from Neutral as higher-voltage AI servers drive aluminium electrolytic capacitor demand and the share-price decline improved valuation.
PT cut from $655 on lower 2026 estimates for weaker advertising and FX. Buy retained.
GS expects about 3% revenue upside, a 4Q guide about 2% above Street and CY26 EPS about 2% above Street.
BESI is likely to remain a funding short on competitive risk and a valuation premium to ASML, following two broker downgrades.

sector_views.rationale: Semis fell eight sessions and hedge funds sold record amounts, but GIR still raises server and AI chip demand forecasts.
US operators are expected to show improving postpaid trends. Nordic names split, with Tele2 the best setup and Telenor and Elisa consensus shorts.
Long and large cycle, but selection should focus on valuation discipline and durable growth.

Verizon Q3 estimates: revenue $35.0bn, EBITDA $13.8bn, 2026 FCF up 10.5% to $22.2bn. AT&T Q3 estimates: revenue $31.8bn, EBITDA $12.5bn, 416k postpaid phone adds.
Spotify Q3 estimate: revenue EUR4.96bn vs guidance and consensus of EUR5.0bn, 305m Premium subscribers, 788m MAUs.
Pearson Q3 organic growth expected about 5.5%. RELX 9M26 organic growth expected about 7%.
META: GIR is broadly in line with Street on Q3/FY26 revenue and 2.4% ahead for 2027 (estimates).

tension_points.bull_case: Gavin Baker argues OpenAI's contract prices are well below spot compute, so repricing will accelerate hyperscaler revenue growth and external financing as a share of the buildout may be peaking. Most see AI demand as fine.
tension_points.bear_case: AI credit spreads for neoclouds and frontier-lab-exposed names have widened and neoclouds fell about 25% on the week. Elevated funding costs and a possible capex growth peak put ROIC and credit quality in focus.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A weak earnings season that fails to arrest the deterioration in sentiment and price momentum.
